headline: Waymo, the robotaxi company owned by Google parent Alphabet, says it will begin testing in Toronto in the coming days and expects to launch a driverless taxi service in the city in 2028.
score_reason: Pool 7 kept (viral rule floor of 7, 41 outlets): a leading robotaxi maker confirmed its first Canadian city, though the service is still about two years away.
importance_line: Toronto riders could get driverless taxis by 2028 and taxi and ride-share drivers face possible job losses, while the real test of snowy winters is still ahead and the city says the permitting law is the province's.
summary: CBC reports that Waymo said on Friday 16 Oct 2026 it is coming to Canada, starting a first testing phase in Toronto that maps local streets and uses trained specialists behind the wheel, after approval to join Ontario's automated vehicle pilot program. Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow said her main concern is safety, and Sidney Givigi, a robotics professor at Queen's University, warned that snow and ice could block the cars' sensors.
notes: CBC full text read. Viral rule applied (41 outlets): score kept at 7. Testing starts with specialists in the driver's seat, so no driverless rides yet; machine_action true because Waymo cars begin operating on Toronto streets in the coming days.
